author: NorthEast News Desk
body: James Rodriguez has returned to Colombian club soccer, signing with Atletico Nacional on a free transfer through June 30, 2027. Reuters reported that the move is the 35-year-old midfielder’s first professional spell in his home country since he left as a teenager.

Rodriguez most recently played for Minnesota United in Major League Soccer. His career has taken him to 14 clubs in 12 countries, including Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Porto and Everton. Atletico Nacional adds a globally recognized playmaker with extensive experience in domestic leagues, continental competitions and international tournaments.

The midfielder became an international star at the 2014 World Cup, winning the Golden Boot as the tournament’s leading scorer. Real Madrid subsequently signed him for 75 million euros. Across his club career he has collected 25 trophies, and he has made 131 appearances for Colombia.

The transfer brings Rodriguez back to a league where he developed before beginning his overseas career with Argentina’s Banfield in 2008. Atletico Nacional will now need to integrate his creativity and experience while managing the physical demands on a veteran player approaching the later stage of his career.
dek: The 35-year-old midfielder signed through June 2027, beginning his first spell in Colombia since leaving the country as a teenager.
headline: James Rodriguez returns to Colombia with Atletico Nacional
